budget_items.topic: Old gas station property (925 Mass Ave) redevelopment
budget_items.what_was_said: The state fulfilled a grant request for a planning consultant to develop redevelopment ideas for the town-owned former gas station property; the select board accepted the consultant's proposal about two months earlier through the Massachusetts Department of Developments program for small towns.

A member noted FRG's quoted price for the town hall project seemed reasonable given Davis-Bacon prevailing wage requirements, and said condo owners at 50 Main Street have obtained quotes from FRG and are getting additional ones before proceeding with steeple repairs.

decisions.decision: The commission will raise the Brooks House warrant-article compliance question at the next select board meeting under comments from other boards/commissions.
William was asked to inform the commission as soon as possible whether he will seek reappointment, since the deadline for appointments is in June.
A master plan steering committee discussion meeting was tentatively set, to be held at Smoke Stacks coffee shop, with the date given inconsistently as June 12th or June 14th at 6:30 p.m.

minutes.summary: The Architectural Preservation District Commission approved a minor window-replacement request at 3 Oak Avenue, then spent most of the meeting on the Brooks House: the chair reported that the Lunenburg Municipal Building Design Committee and the Select Board have not complied with a November town-meeting warrant directing a plot plan and consultation process, and the commission voted to press the Select Board on this at its next meeting. Members also reviewed town hall and steeple repair project status, historical commission quorum and survey work, APDC reappointments, a land-use-director vacancy, and a tentative master plan steering committee meeting date.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to press the Select Board over a November town-meeting warrant on the Brooks House that its building design committee has not followed.
The chair said the Design Committee and Select Board have not completed the plot plan and consultation process voters directed.
The commission approved a window-replacement request at 3 Oak Avenue without requiring a full certificate of alteration.
Members set a tentative date for a master plan steering committee discussion, though the minutes give it inconsistently as June 12th or 14th.

why_it_matters: A warrant article passed at town meeting is a voter directive; a board or committee not following it is a compliance question a resident can raise at the next Select Board meeting.
The determination-of-applicability process at 3 Oak Avenue shows how the commission handles small alteration requests in the historic district without a full certificate hearing.
Land-use-director and commission-seat vacancies discussed here touch who reviews future applications in the district.
